extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and reviewers for NIH NIAID Phase II STTR grants (small business + collaborating investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and review criteria used to evaluate NIH/NIAID Phase II (Type 2 R42/R44) STTR grant applications for drug discovery and development. Covers the standard NIH review criteria (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) plus human/animal protections, budget, resource sharing, and scoring procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: The overall impact of the proposal to develop effective therapies for RNA viruses ... is very high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes how the project’s strengths and weaknesses combine to affect the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field and/or lead toward the stated product development goals (e.g., nomination of a clinical candidate). Reviewers average overall scores (1-9), multiply by 10 to produce the impact/priority score. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting and are not discussed or directly calculated into the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate unmet need (e.g., lack of approved therapies), potential public health impact (including bioterror implications), strength of scientific premise, and whether success would change clinical practice or enable IND-enabling studies. Consider preliminary data such as in vivo proof-of-concept and applicability to related pathogens (e.g., potential relevance to SARS-CoV-2). Note explicit Strengths and Weaknesses as provided by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s): Are the PD(s)/PI(s), collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess qualifications, track record in relevant disciplines (medicinal chemistry, virology, computation), history of productive collaboration, and presence of essential expertise (including business development for commercialization). Note any missing expertise or concerns about team composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice by utilizing novel concepts, approaches, or technologies?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate novelty of mechanism (e.g., blocking host Nedd4:PPxY interactions), novelty of small-molecule series, and potential for broad-spectrum antiviral indications. Note whether any aspects claimed as 'new' are unclear and represent a potential weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess experimental design, feasibility, rigor (screening cascade, criteria for success/go/no-go decisions), execution plan (Aims 1–4), ADME/PK/tox strategies, in vitro/in vivo testing plans (including BSL-4 studies), and acknowledgement/mitigation of lead optimization challenges (e.g., high logD, low solubility). Consider whether Phase II is contingent on completing Phase I objectives. Look for clearly delineated go/no-go criteria, timelines, and plans such as prodrug strategies when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment: Will the scientific environment contribute to the probability of success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate institutional resources, facilities (including access to ABS-L4 labs), CRO resources, collaborations, and whether the environment provides necessary infrastructure for IND-directed studies and BSL-4 work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II (Type 2 R42 and Type 2 R44) Acceptability / Progress from Phase I
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase II: Acceptable — The progress made from the Phase I study shows robust data with POC in vivo reduction of Marburg virus challenged mouse models and a clear product development plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Phase II applications, evaluate whether Phase I deliverables provide sufficient proof-of-concept to justify Phase II aims, existence of a target product profile (TPP), go/no-go decision framework, commercialization strategy, intellectual property protections, and likelihood to nominate an IND-ready candidate. Consider budget statutory limits and whether a waiver is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Protections for Human Subjects: Acceptable Risks and Adequate Protections
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess justification for human subjects use (e.g., blood collection to isolate PBMCs), inclusion/exclusion criteria, age/gender/race distributions justified scientifically, informed consent procedures (risks explained by PI or physician representative), monitoring of participant recruitment, and documentation that risks are minimized and privacy protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Plans (Sex/Gender, Race/Ethnicity, Inclusion Across the Lifespan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion Plans: Sex/Gender, Race/Ethnicity, and Inclusion/Exclusion Based on Age are justified scientifically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that distribution of sex/gender and race/ethnicity is scientifically justified and that age ranges (e.g., adults 18–50) are appropriate for the aims. Ensure recruitment monitoring and non-discrimination statements are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertebrate Animals: YES, all criteria addressed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require justifications for animal use, descriptions of protections during studies, methods of euthanasia where appropriate, and appropriate documentation for DMPK and in vivo efficacy studies. Confirm that animal care/use protocols are in place and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether biohazard risks are identified and minimized, and that appropriate biosafety practices and facilities are in place for proposed studies (including BSL-2 and BSL-4 work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm compliance with select agent regulations where applicable and appropriate institutional approvals and containment plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess plans for sharing data, reagents, and other resources; determine whether plans are adequate for community access and follow NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources: Acceptable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for plans and evidence to authenticate cell lines, biological reagents, and chemical compounds used in the study to ensure reproducibility and validity of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget and Period of Support: Recommend as Requested
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee reviews whether requested direct costs are justified and within programmatic/statutory limits for Phase II STTRs. Administrative note: the budget shown is the requested budget and has not been adjusted to reflect reviewer recommendations; if an award is planned, institute grants management staff will calculate final costs. Note any recommended modifications, overlaps, or budget waiver election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee Budget Recommendations / Administrative Budget Note
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Budget Note: The budget shown is the requested budget and has not been adjusted to reflect any recommendations made by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If award is planned, grants management staff will calculate costs based on committee recommendations. Reviewers may recommend budget as requested or suggest modifications; note statutory guidelines for Phase II STTR budgets and whether a waiver is elected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability Determinations (e.g., Acceptable/Unacceptable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinations such as 'Acceptable' for Protections for Human Subjects, Biohazards, Resource Sharing, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers explicitly mark sections as Acceptable/YES/Acceptable Risks and Adequate Protections. Use these determinations to indicate compliance with NIH policies and whether additional clarifications are needed prior to award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and Review Process / Impact Score Calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring/Review Process: Impact/priority score calculated by averaging overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some applications receive percentile rankings. For full details see NIH peer review process guidance (link provided). Understand that criterion scores (Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, Environment) inform discussion but the overall impact score is the primary numeric outcome.
